task.name: Land the last gate-green commit instead of failing the story when a final iteration turns the gate red
task.story_text:
A story can be driven from a passing, approved state into a failing one by its own
last dev iteration, and forge then discards all of it.

Observed in sprint issues-248,245,246,231, story #246:

- Gate run 2 returned PASS ("iOS tests passed", full build + unit tests) at commit
  2dd9f135.
- The review cycle that followed returned APPROVE with a single P2 finding.
- The dev spent its third and final iteration on that in-scope P2, which changed
  restored-session reconcile semantics. It could validate only with formatter and
  linter, so the change went into the gate unexercised.
- Gate run 3 returned FAIL with three failing tests, all on the semantics the P2
  fix altered.
- The dev iteration pool was now 3/3 with hit_limit true, so nothing remained to
  recover, and no further review cycle opened.
- The story was reported FAILED, its work discarded, and the failure classified as
  iteration_exhaustion with the operator-facing recommendation "raise the iteration
  budget for #246 or narrow its scope, then re-run".

Forge was holding a known-good commit at the moment it declared total failure. The
P2 policy that produced this is deliberate and worth keeping: an unfixed P2 becomes
a review finding later and is re-fixed from scratch at higher cost. The gap is that
attempting a P2 currently risks the entire story with no floor under it.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a story's gate passed at some commit and a later iteration leaves the gate
  failing with no dev iterations remaining, forge can land the last gate-green
  commit rather than reporting the story failed.
- The landed outcome is distinguishable in the summary and audit from a story that
  passed on its final iteration, and names the commit landed and the work dropped.
- The operator can tell, from the summary alone, that a later iteration was
  discarded and why.
- A story with no gate-green commit in its history is unaffected and still fails.

## Example

For #246 the sprint summary reported:

```
FAILED — iteration_exhaustion (1)
  #246  $3.30  25m
       primary:      iteration_exhaustion
       contributing: dev_iteration_limit
```

with the recommendation to raise the iteration budget. The desired outcome is
instead to land 2dd9f135 — already gate-green and review-approved — drop the P2
commit that broke it, and report the story as landed with the P2 outstanding, so
the P2 returns as a normal finding rather than costing the story.

The same run should instead have reported:

```
LANDED (1 of 1)
  ✓ #246  $3.30  25m   landed at 2dd9f135 (gate-green, review-approved)
       outstanding:  1 P2, dropped from this story and returned as a normal finding
```

handoff.summary: Added coordinator/gate_green_salvage.py, which lands the last review-approved, gate-green commit when a later dev iteration turns the gate red with no dev iterations left. REVIEW captures a checkpoint when an approval routes into P2 cleanup, gated on ReviewedCommitVerification.state == gate_passed so a gate_stale approval is never landable. The engine converts a terminal GATE_FAIL escalation into the existing deferred landing path (result AND state move to DONE/pending_integration, superseded escalation recorded, decline reasons recorded when salvage is unsafe). land_story resets the branch to the checkpoint before the normal merge path and fails closed if it cannot, and detects the merge-pr rebase case so no record claims a SHA GitHub never merged. Batch-group leaders are ineligible because member reviews run against the shared branch after the leader returns. landing_record, the per-run audit (schema 31 to 32 with a reader-side migration), and the sprint digest render it as a distinct outcome naming the landed commit, the dropped commits, and why.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A story with no gate-green commit in its history is unaffected and still fails.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Salvage returns the original CoordinatorResult untouched with no state mutation; failure classification is unchanged. Covered by test_gate_never_green_still_fails and test_no_checkpoint_still_fails_unchanged.

story_deviations: AC1 says 'the gate passed at some commit'; the implementation requires that commit to also have been approved by a review cycle whose verification state is gate_passed. A gate-green commit no reviewer approved is not landed — merge-pr fails closed without a review result, and resetting onto an unreviewed tree is the risk the plan reviewer flagged. Such cases are recorded as a gate_green_never_approved decline rather than silently taking the old path.

Batch-group leaders are excluded from salvage. A batch branch carries other stories' commits and member reviews run against it after the leader's coordinator pass returns, so a later reset would review one tree and land another. Recorded as a batch_group_leader decline.
deferred_items: No operator notification is sent when a salvage supersedes an escalation — _escalate_notify has already fired by then, so the operator may see an escalate ping for a story that reports LANDED. The supersession is recorded in the audit and as a gate_green_salvage structured event, but a follow-up notify was out of scope.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2, advisory cleanup on the one carried P2. The P2 asks whether restricting salvage to review-approved gate-green commits (rather than all gate-green commits, as AC1 words it) is intentional; it is, and the finding permits no code change in that case. I documented the narrowing where it is enforced: record_gate_green_checkpoint's docstring now enumerates both narrowings against AC1 with the rationale for each (merge-pr fails closed without a ReviewResult, and resetting onto an unreviewed tree would ship unreviewed code to escape a failure; plus the separate same-commit requirement that rejects gate_stale approvals), and the module docstring names the AC1 gap and points at the gate_green_never_approved decline that keeps it operator-visible. I also fixed an accuracy bug in that decline message, which is the mechanism making the narrowing visible: it read the commit from state.last_gate_commit (the commit the LATEST gate judged, i.e. the failing one on this feature's PASS-then-FAIL shape) and the verdict from state.gate_decisions (which gains a synthetic PASS on the story gate:-override skip path, so a suppressed gate reported as green). New _last_gate_green_commit reads state.validation_runs, which records result, commit, and skipped together; absence in legacy pre-#2358 records reads as no-gate-green rather than as a pass. No behavior outside the decline message changed; the salvage decision, rollback, landing, audit, and digest paths are untouched from iteration 1.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 treats last_gate_decision == PASS plus last_gate_commit as sufficient proof of a review-approved gate-green checkpoint, but those fields do not prove that REVIEW approved that exact SHA. In validate_phase.py, _record_gate_run records HEAD before the post-PASS dirty-worktree auto-commit; review_phase.py then reviews the new HEAD, and ReviewedCommitVerification.derive in state.py correctly labels the mismatch gate_stale. The proposed guard could therefore reset to the pre-auto-commit parent or label a stale-gate approval as landable, carrying the plan's stated gate-green/review-approved risk.
  Suggestion: Require the approving ReviewCycleMetadata to have verification.state == gate_passed and reviewed_commit == verification.gate_commit, and checkpoint that exact SHA. Add a negative seam test for a PASS followed by the existing post-gate auto-commit/gate_stale path.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 records the checkpoint SHA as landed_commit and then invokes the existing merge-pr path. completion._merge_pr always runs _step_fetch_rebase before force-pushing; when origin/base has advanced, rebase rewrites the checkpoint SHA. The audit and digest would then claim that the original gate-green SHA was landed even though GitHub landed a different commit, violating the commit-naming acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: Track checkpoint_commit separately from the actual post-rebase landed_commit. Resolve and record HEAD after rebase, and render both when they differ, or introduce a landing path that preserves the checkpoint identity. Test merge-pr salvage with an advanced base branch.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan misses the shared-branch caller in sprint/runner.py::_run_batch_group. A salvaged batch leader returns pending_integration, then all non-leader member reviews run against the still gate-red HEAD; only afterward does _attempt_integration call land_story and reset the shared branch to the checkpoint. Forge can therefore review one tree and land another, possibly dropping work attributed to a batch member.
  Suggestion: Either make salvage ineligible for batch-group leaders, or perform the checkpoint rollback before _run_batch_group launches member reviews and rebuild the shared handoff/commit attribution from the retained checkpoint. Add a batch seam test proving every member is reviewed against the exact tree ultimately landed.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The escalation side effects fire before the salvage helper can run. validate_phase.py:1279-1284 already emits the escalate structured event, calls _escalate_notify, sets state.error, and _apply_block_route has mutated routing state — all before _run_validate_phase returns ESCALATE to engine.py:788. Step 3 also mutates only the CoordinatorResult, leaving state.phase = Phase.ESCALATE (set at validate_phase.py:1270), which is what audit/state serializers read (sprint/audit.py:1702).
  Suggestion: Set state.phase = Phase.DONE alongside the result mutation, and append a salvage audit entry that explicitly supersedes the escalate event so the audit does not carry an escalation for a story reported LANDED. Consider whether the operator notification needs a follow-up 'salvaged' notify.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1 (gate-green vs gate-green+approved) is only partly retired. The plan's narrowing is the right safety call — merge-pr already fails closed without a review (completion.py:1534 missing-review) — but AC1 is written on 'gate passed at some commit', so a gate-green-but-never-approved commit will silently take the old FAILED path with no operator-visible reason.
  Suggestion: Record the near-miss: when a gate-green commit exists but no approve-equivalent checkpoint was captured, log/record why salvage was declined so the operator can distinguish 'nothing to salvage' from 'salvageable but unapproved'.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 names src/theforge/coordinator/resume_persistence.py as the sidecar home, but last_gate_commit/last_gate_decision are persisted by save_trajectory_state/load_trajectory_state in src/theforge/coordinator/run_setup.py:168 and :228.
  Suggestion: Extend run_setup.py's trajectory sidecar; reuse the existing _serialize_review_result/_deserialize_review_result helpers there (already used for hygiene_escalation_prior_review) to persist the checkpoint's ReviewResult.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 7 lists tests/test_sprint_landing_record.py and tests/test_cli_sprint_digest.py as create, but both files already exist (as does tests/test_landing_record.py).
  Suggestion: Append the new cases to the existing files rather than overwriting them.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 2 (branch reset before merge-pr) is mitigated in Step 4 but the Step 7 git test is described only as 'only the checkpoint commit merges'. The merge-pr path reaches GitHub through _step_force_push (completion.py:671) and past the already-merged / zero-delta guards (completion.py:1218, :1310), which read the worktree HEAD sha.
  Suggestion: Cover merge-pr explicitly, not just local merge: assert the PR head becomes the checkpoint after reset and that the already-merged guard does not misfire on the moved ref.

finding_registry.description: The implementation salvages only gate-green commits that were also approved by a review cycle (where ReviewedCommitVerification.state == "gate_passed"), not all gate-green commits. Commits the gate passed on but no review approved are recorded as gate_green_never_approved declines and left to fail.

When the only prior PASS in validation_runs came from an advisory override and the merge-authority gate later failed terminally, the salvage audit recorded a gate_green_never_approved near-miss saying the gate passed at the advisory commit.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
